messages:
maya: Heads up — we need a quick decision on how Dedicated -> Hosted overflow should surface in the Console. Customer asked for permanent fallback; concern about tenant isolation and quota charging.
jonathan: Are you talking about automatic overflow when a dedicated pool is saturated? We currently have a circuit that reroutes to hosted cheaper variants and we emit a coarse metric 'overflow.route'.
lee: +1 that metric is too coarse. Can't see which tenant, which model_variant, or whether support manually forced it.
sophia: We aggregated intentionally to avoid any content or PII leakage. But customers want per-tenant telemetry (latency/cost) for SLA reconciliation. Need a safe telemetry schema. :thinking:
dan: Proposal: emit per-tenant hashed_id + model_variant + routing_decision in telemetry, but scrub prompt/response. That should give traceability without exposing content.
maya: That sounds reasonable. Product also wants a Console toggle 'Allow hosted fallback' per customer and a 'last overflow' row with reason and cost delta visible to admins.
jonathan: API semantics: falling back should bill to hosted usage, not dedicated. Also quota enforcement: we must prevent cross-tenant quota leakage during bursts.
sophia: On quotas — we could keep a strict per-tenant token budget and provide a fast path: if dedicated exhausted and tenant allows fallback, create ephemeral hosted billing entry tagged to tenant. Need to decide rate-limit windows (second vs minute).
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: New feature branch created: feat/overflow-telemetry-182345 — e2e tests queued.
lee: Ops question: how do we surface model_variant fallback in logs? Example: tenant pins neoX-20b dedicated; fallback could go to quantized-20b-hosted. We should show mapping in audit logs and in the Console.
dan: I'll sketch an event schema we can stream to kafka/telemetry-prod. No prompt text, only routing metadata. Example schema:
```
{
  "event_type": "routing_decision",
  "tenant_hash": "hmac_sha256(customer_id, env_salt)",
  "request_id": "uuid",
  "decision": "allow_fallback|block",
  "source_pool": "dedicated-us-west-1",
  "target_pool": "hosted-quant20b",
  "model_fallback": "quant20b",
  "cost_estimate": "0.0025",
  "latency_ms": "int",
  "reason": "capacity_exhausted|policy_override|manual",
  "timestamp": "iso"
}
```
jonathan: We need an API endpoint to collect routing events or wire them directly from the router into our pipeline. Maybe POST /v1/routing_events with idempotency key. Idempotency important for retries.
maya: UX: show per-route last 7 days overflow count + cost delta + controls: hard block (no fallback) or soft allow (notify + fallback). Product is leaning hard-block opt-in, soft-allow default for enterprise.
sophia: Security review: ensure tenant_hash can't be reversed. Use HMAC with customer id + rotateable salt. Document rotation plan and access controls. :lock:
lee: Performance: we can't HMAC by calling KMS per request. Use local HMAC cache with in-memory keys rotated from KMS every N hours. Telemetry should be batched and fire-and-forget, not blocking inference path.
dan: Rollout plan idea: feature flag gated, canary to 3 customers, then 1% traffic ramp, then 10%, add alert if fallback rate > 2% for any tenant. Also emit alert when cost delta > threshold.
maya: Action items: dan implement schema + producer; lee add per-tenant metric keys and Console plumbing; jonathan spec API endpoint + idempotency semantics; sophia write security note and rotation plan; maya mock Console UI and coordinate canary list. Sync tomorrow 09:30.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: RFC link: https://redwood/internal/rfc/overflow-routing — please add notes to the RFC if you agree.

(emoji reactions: :+1: from jonathan, :eyes: from lee)
